The People Service Delivery (PSD) team's mission is to run a high-performing, people-focused service delivery organization. Leading with care and empathy, we develop efficient processes, systems, and programs. We aim to ensure employees feel heard and have the resources and support they need during the most important moments so they can do impactful work. The People Service Delivery Lead sits at the intersection of people operations domain expertise and hands-on engineering. This role owns large-scale transformation programs end to end, and, unlike a traditional program role, also contributes to designing and building the solutions those programs depend on. This lead reads HR, payroll, and people-operations workflows fluently, identifies where the seams and inefficiencies are, and then helps architect tooling solutions that close them. Working closely with leaders across People Operations, executive sponsors, engineering, and other key XFN stakeholders, this lead challenges assumptions and the status quo to improve processes, reduce barriers, and mitigate risks. Much of the work is greenfield: problems arrive without a playbook, and this lead defines the path as they walk it. This person does not need to have the “correct” answer to everything. What matters is the ability to quickly drive the conversation toward a productive solution by bringing together the right people, process, and technology, including building a working prototype when that is the fastest way to create clarity. A key expectation of this role is to be an active driver of AI adoption and creative problem-solving in operations. This lead looks for opportunities to responsibly use AI and automation to reduce manual work, improve consistency, accelerate resolution times, and enhance the employee experience while ensuring strong governance, quality, and appropriate handling of sensitive information.

Responsibilities

  • Own development, organization, and execution of large, complex business and operational programs from inception through delivery, with little to no oversight; own the program roadmap and scoping, making tradeoffs to optimize time-to-release and clearly communicating goals, roles, responsibilities, and desired outcomes
  • Deliver tooling that removes manual effort from people operations workflows
  • Partner with Engineering to shape system design and technical direction, translating people operations needs into clear requirements
  • Participate in design and solution reviews, holding a high-quality bar for what the team ships
  • Deconstruct end-to-end employee lifecycle journeys (from hire through movement, leave, and exit) to identify seams, handoff failure points, and automation opportunities across teams and systems, then build the solutions that address them. Drive AI-enabled operational improvement, including identifying use cases for automation, workflow optimization, knowledge management, and case deflection, balancing efficiency with employee care and quality outcomes
  • Improve efficiency and quality of systems and operations through end-to-end process frameworks and optimization initiatives, and design the change management that drives adoption of new processes, systems, or tooling, including training and communication plans for all levels, locations, and XFN partners
  • Partner with HR Tech, engineering teams, and vendors to identify, build, and implement appropriate technology solutions; oversee system integration efforts and ensure smooth transition and adoption
  • Identify, escalate, and mitigate program risk proactively rather than reactively
  • Move fluidly between audiences (SMEs, payroll leadership, engineering peers, and skip-level leadership), simplifying complex technical concepts for non-technical groups without losing precision, and maintaining open, candid, and trusting working relationships
  • Monitor stabilization of changes to ensure processes and systems are executed per design

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in managing large-scale, global transformation or continuous improvement initiatives aimed at improving business processes, systems, and operations, with demonstrable business results
  • Domain knowledge of HR, payroll, or people-operations processes, or demonstrated experience in ramping quickly into a complex operational domain
  • Experience designing or operating HR processes spanning multiple stages of the employee lifecycle (e.g., hire/onboarding, movement, leaves and time away, compensation and payroll events, and offboarding), with an understanding of how upstream decisions create downstream operational load
  • Experience operating independently through ambiguity on greenfield problems, navigating competing and shifting priorities to maintain momentum, and delivering results in a detail-oriented, highly organized manner
  • Experience problem-solving using data, translating thorough examination and analysis into action
  • Experience working in an XFN environment: building relationships, consensus building, and motivating teams at all levels, technical and non-technical, to get colleagues on board with the benefits of transformational change

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge and understanding of the tech and software industry's business models and core processes
  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Experience in understanding and facilitating change in a dynamic environment: handling challenges and pushback from senior stakeholders
  • Experience in requirement analysis techniques and methodologies, and delivering business value through process improvement in a high-tech operations space
  • Comfortable working in a modern web stack (TypeScript, React) environment and able to hold substantive technical conversations with engineering partners
  • Bachelor's degree in a technical, business, or operations discipline, or equivalent experience

Meta is seeking a data center lead building engineer to join our data center facility operations team. Our data centers serve as the foundation upon which our software operates to meet the demands of our customers. The Lead Building Engineer will be a part of the Facility Operations team responsible for operating and maintaining critical systems in our data centers. They will be an individual contributor who provides day-to-day coordination and oversight of work over one or more buildings totaling around 70+ MW critical capacity. The Lead Building Engineer will report to a Critical Operations Manager and will be expected to maintain a comprehensive understanding of the state of the data center buildings or property they oversee. The candidate will need experience across technical disciplines such as electrical generation, electrical distribution, cooling technologies, building control, and fire protection systems.

Responsibilities

  • Oversee the work for one or more 30MW+ data centers to ensure schedule deconfliction, work priority, maintenance compliance, procedural compliance, and team readiness
  • Schedule and supervise vendors/subcontractors during equipment/systems maintenance and services
  • Perform hands-on operations and maintenance, which includes all physical and administrative operations tasks, services, and maintenance, in accordance with site processes and procedures, to ensure optimal uptime, efficiency, and safety in accordance with site standards without disruption to the business
  • Review all operating procedures, serve as the final approval authority on some procedures based on internal standards
  • Support incident management, root cause analysis, and corrective action closure for any operational issues that arise in the data center
  • Achieve and maintain a high level of technical knowledge regarding data center infrastructure and operations. Successfully complete the personnel qualification standards (PQS) training
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of Meta policies and standards and follow standards in all work
  • Provide in-the-field training to Critical Facility Engineers and support the identification of training needs across the team
  • Ensure the accuracy of work orders in the Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) system (Hexagon)
  • Collaborate with peer Lead Building Engineers to deconflict work across campus and maintain consistency in operations between buildings
  • Provide technical expertise and assistance as required
  • Regularly inspect equipment, buildings, safety routes and grounds to check or identify any abnormal or unsafe conditions or faults
  • Troubleshoot, evaluate, and recommend system upgrades
  • Order parts and supplies for maintenance and repairs through the procurement and inventory management system
  • Escalate issues to facility management appropriately and in a timely manner

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in electrical, HVAC, mechanical, controls, or other technical maintenance fields
  • Proficient with maintenance management programs
  • Proficient with computer systems, including documents, spreadsheets, and email
  • Ability to regularly walk job site areas of flat and uneven terrain
  • Ability to work at varying heights and from ladders
  • Ability to use hands and fingers
  • Ability to reach, push, pull with hands, arms, and shoulders
  • Ability to stoop, kneel, crouch, and crawl
  • Ability to lift and/or otherwise move forty-five pounds or more
  • Ability to sit or stand at a workstation for extended periods of time

Preferred Qualifications

  • Knowledge of mechanical, electrical, and life safety monitoring and control systems typically used in critical environments
  • 7+ years of experience in a data center or other critical environment (pharma, clean room, medical, power production, etc.)
  • Bachelor’s Degree, Associates Degree, Trade Certification or state licensure in Electrical or Mechanical (HVAC)
  • Experience in interpreting blueprints/CAD drawings

Meta's Infrastructure Silicon organization is building custom ASICs to power the compute demands of AI, data center, and next-generation platform workloads. We are looking for an experienced Silicon Validation Engineer to join our team, working across the full silicon lifecycle from early pre-silicon design input and FPGA emulation to post-silicon bring-up, characterization, and deployment in the production fleet. You will play a central role in validating custom silicon, driving emulation bring-up, and leading debug efforts across hardware, firmware, and software layers to ensure successful product delivery. Your work will directly influence the reliability and performance of Meta's custom infrastructure chips at scale.

Responsibilities

  • Work across all aspects of the silicon lifecycle to deliver reliable, performant silicon - from early architecture and design input, through pre-silicon test readiness and validation, to post-silicon bring-up, characterization, and fleet deployment
  • Define and execute silicon validation strategies, including test plans, coverage models, regression frameworks, and productization readiness criteria
  • Develop and maintain emulation infrastructure for custom silicon, including FPGA-based emulation platform bring-up and configuration
  • Partition and map RTL designs onto emulation platforms, optimizing for timing closure, resource utilization, and debug visibility
  • Build and maintain software, scripting, and automation infrastructure for validation and emulation workflows, including silicon diagnostics, performance analysis, debug tooling, job scheduling, and results analysis across bare-metal and full-stack systems
  • Debug complex hardware, firmware, and software interactions across RTL, firmware, and software layers; root-cause, resolve, and remediate silicon issues across the product lifecycle
  • Partner with RTL design and verification engineers to identify and resolve functional bugs prior to tape-out
  • Ensure continuity between pre- and post-silicon environments so that emulation accurately models silicon behavior and validation content transitions cleanly into lab and data center bring-up
  • Understand production system use cases to improve silicon validation, and feed insights from the production fleet back into next-generation architecture and design
  • Evaluate and integrate new validation and emulation tools, methodologies, and platform capabilities to improve throughput and debug efficiency
  • Lead end-to-end validation efforts, driving strategy, planning, execution, and post-silicon enablement and provide technical guidance to peers on validation methodology, debug techniques, and infrastructure best practices

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 6+ years of experience in ASIC/SoC development cycles with pre-silicon and/or post-silicon validation, hardware verification, or FPGA-based emulation for custom silicon
  • Experience troubleshooting, debug, and analytics for silicon products, including debugging hardware-software interactions using waveform viewers, logic analyzers, and hardware debug probes
  • Experience with ASIC design or development, emulation, and post-silicon validation
  • Experience developing automation scripts and test infrastructure in Python, C/C++,
  • Experience collaborating with internal and external partners across RTL design, verification, firmware, software, and systems teams in a custom silicon environment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with RTL partitioning, FPGA synthesis, and timing closure on large-scale emulation platforms such as Palladium, Veloce, or Zebu
  • Experience working with emulation/FPGA platforms for test content development, debug, and post-silicon enablement
  • Experience with post-silicon bring-up and transitioning validation content from emulation to silicon environments
  • Familiarity with SystemVerilog, UVM, or formal verification methodologies as complements to emulation-based validation
  • Experience with hardware description and simulation tools such as VCS, Xcelium, or Questa
  • Experience with infrastructure or data center silicon domains such as networking ASICs, AI accelerators, or storage controllers
  • Experience with some of the following modules/domains: PCIe, Networking, Ethernet, Flash, Memory, CPU, GPU, DRAM (LP/DDR4/5 and/or HBM)
  • Understanding of embedded systems, including common bus protocols such as I2C, SPI, USB, and/or PCIe
  • Experience with Linux systems and server systems management
  • Experience in application and host driver development, including RDMA Gen Driver, DPDK, or Meta RoCE/RoCEv2, for NIC product validation

As a Prototyping Engineer within the multidisciplinary Proto Make Team, you will employ your expertise in problem solving and model making to accelerate product development across Meta's hardware organization. You will collaborate with teams within Hardware Engineering, Research and Development, and Industrial Design. These projects cover a wide variety of technical challenges unique to Meta's hardware portfolio, including Meta Quest, Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, AI wearables, robotics, and beyond. As the next stage of consumer hardware moves closer to the body, rapid soft element exploration has become exponentially more vital in creating human first technologies. This role requires expertise in molding and casting for use in prototype hardware informing early design decisions. Knowledge of silicone, polyurethanes, additive manufacturing and novel fabrication processes will be crucial in creating fast prototypes in all shapes and sizes. You will work throughout the hardware lifecycle with a particular focus on prototype ideation and early-to-mid stage development. This is a casting and molding specialist role. Your primary craft is mold design and construction and the casting of silicones, urethanes, and foams — you will independently own the most demanding casting and molding work in the lab, adding genuine specialist capacity and redundancy rather than task-level coverage. As is typical of any model making role here, that work is delivered inside complete Industrial Design models, so you will routinely incorporate components from CNC machining, 3D printing, and 2D cutting to carry a build end-to-end. You will also partner with the Casting & Molding leads to raise the maturity of how the function runs — tooling, SOPs, and workflow that scale beyond a handful of individuals. Our team is constantly growing and you will be relied upon to help define team direction and be motivated to improve the effectiveness of our tools and processes from each project to the next.

Responsibilities

  • Complex casting & molding: Independently run the lab's most demanding casting and molding projects in silicones, urethanes, resins and foams, mixed, degassed, cast and cured to spec. Finish cast prototypes to rigorous cosmetic standards. Partner with the Casting and Molding leads on the hardest new problems, adding specialist capacity and redundancy to a critical function
  • Mold design & construction: Design and build 3D printed and traditional molds, including multi-part and complex geometries. Design and adapt molds, fixtures and model components in Autodesk Fusion instead of only building to spec
  • Complete models: Take designs from concept to finished physical model, pulling in CNC, 3D printed and 2D cut parts and using both internal and external manufacturing. Bring core model making skills: high-quality finishing, part prep, scratch building, color mixing and strong material knowledge
  • Soft goods prototyping: Quickly explore cast soft components for products worn on the body. Work with Industrial Design, Engineering and Research to solve complex design and UX problems and shape early design decisions
  • Fast, parallel iteration: Manage multiple concurrent projects by prioritizing work based on impact, deadlines, and stakeholder needs, keeping parts flowing for fast design cycles
  • Process improvement & documentation: Try new materials and methods, then turn what works into standard tooling, SOPs and workflows so the function can scale. Build and maintain a knowledge base and clear teaching docs for molding, casting, finishing and material handling
  • Mentorship: Share best practices and give hands-on guidance to team members and CW staff, helping new people ramp up on core skills and lab safety
  • Lab organization: Keep the lab clean and organized and keep improving it. Own inventory, housekeeping, materials ordering and digital workflow and inventory records

At Meta, we're building the future of human connection and the technology that enables it, continuously inventing for the next generation of experiences. To move toward advanced machine intelligence, we're enabling AI to go beyond vision and interact with the physical world. As we move closer to a future with intelligent robots and advanced AI models, we're hiring talent across robotics hardware, system software, machine perception, and artificial intelligence. You'll tackle open problems in robotics and AI, with the opportunity to shape new ways people connect around the world. Hardware fails at the seams — where mechanical, electrical, firmware, and software meet, and again where a working prototype meets a repeatable build process. This role owns both. You will bring up new hardware in the lab, then carry it forward into a manufacturable, testable, scalable product: defining the build and test process, standing up the stations that verify it, and driving yield, throughput, and first-pass quality as volumes grow. It is a deliberately blended role for someone who can debug a one-off unit on the bench in the morning and improve a process that has to work on the hundredth unit in the afternoon.

Responsibilities

  • Lead bring-up of new platforms, actuator generations, and subassemblies: power-on, firmware flashing, calibration, sensor validation, closed-loop tuning, and first motion
  • Integrate subsystems end to end — actuators, encoders, IMUs, tactile and force sensing, cameras, power distribution, comms buses (CAN/CAN-FD, EtherCAT, SPI/I2C, Ethernet), and onboard compute
  • Own system-level behavior and interfaces: define and hold the mechanical, electrical, and software interface contracts between subsystems, and arbitrate the tradeoffs when they conflict
  • Debug hard, ambiguous, cross-domain problems — intermittent faults, noise and grounding issues, timing and latency, thermal behavior, mechanical compliance masquerading as a control problem
  • Write and modify embedded firmware and host-side tooling (C/C++, Python) for bring-up, calibration, diagnostics, and data capture
  • Own the integration test plan: define what 'working' means per subsystem, automate the checks, and keep them passing as the design changes underneath them
  • Characterize system performance against spec — accuracy, bandwidth, torque and thermal envelope, latency, power — and feed the gaps back to design as concrete requirements
  • Build the data path: logging, telemetry, and analysis tooling that turns robot runs and test builds into duty-cycle, performance, and reliability evidence the team can design against
  • Contribute to functional safety — including risk assessment, safety review participation, and validation of safe-state behavior
  • Carry your own designs and integrations into a repeatable build: define the assembly and calibration sequence, the acceptance criteria at each stage, and the work instructions behind them
  • Design, build, and deploy test stations and end-of-line test: fixturing, harnesses, DAQ, load application, station software, limits, and the data logging behind them
  • Drive first-pass yield and cycle time on the builds you own: find the top failure contributors and close them with design, firmware, process, or fixture changes
  • Establish calibration and traceability at scale — per-unit calibration data, serialization, and a data trail that supports later failure analysis and field investigations
  • Bring DFM/DFA and DFT thinking into design reviews — testability, tolerance realism, and assembly practicality, pushed in before the design is locked
  • Support NPI builds hands-on (EVT/DVT/PVT) and partner with CMs and suppliers on process transfer, station duplication, and incoming quality; travel to build sites as needed
  • Partner with design ME/EE/FW, controls, quality, manufacturing engineering, and lab operations; document interfaces and processes so integration knowledge does not live in one person's head

Minimum Qualifications

  • BS in Mechatronics, Electrical, Mechanical, Robotics, Manufacturing, or Computer Engineering, or equivalent
  • 7+ years building, debugging, and transitioning real electromechanical systems from prototype into volume — systems that had to work outside a simulator and be built more than once
  • Proficiency in C/C++ for embedded targets and Python for tooling, station software, and analysis
  • AI-native working style: uses AI coding agents and LLM tooling as a default part of the job — to scaffold bring-up scripts, station software, and log-analysis pipelines, mine large run and build datasets for failure signatures, and draft work instructions, test plans, and interface documentation — while independently validating every AI-produced result against the hardware and the data before it drives a build or a design decision
  • Hands-on electronics skills: reading schematics, bring-up of custom boards, soldering, harness fabrication, oscilloscope/logic-analyzer/DMM debugging
  • Demonstrated ownership of a test station or automated test process you designed, deployed, and maintained for others to use
  • Practical experience with at least one real-time comms bus (CAN/CAN-FD, EtherCAT, RS-485, SPI/I2C) and with motor drives or servo systems
  • Working understanding of closed-loop control: PID, feedforward, current/velocity/position cascades, filtering, and why a tuned gain set stops working when the mechanics change
  • Mechanical literacy: reading GD&T-annotated drawings, CAD (Creo, SolidWorks, or similar), tolerance stack-ups, fastener and preload basics
  • Experience writing work instructions, test plans, and process documentation others actually follow
  • Disciplined software habits — version control, code review, reproducible scripts

Preferred Qualifications

  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
  • Experience in a fast prototype environment where you specified and procured your own hardware
  • Manufacturing engineering depth: yield and Pareto analysis, SPC, process capability (Cp/Cpk), MSA/Gage R&R, PFMEA, control plans, 8D
  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Experience bringing up humanoid, legged, or high-DOF robots, or high-performance actuators
  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
  • Functional safety experience: ISO 13849 / ISO 10218 / IEC 61508, safety relays and STO, risk assessment authoring
  • Motor control depth: FOC, commutation and encoder calibration, torque-constant and friction characterization
  • Experience through a full NPI cycle (EVT → DVT → PVT → MP) on an electromechanical product, including CM or supplier process transfer
  • EMC/EMI, grounding and shielding, and power-integrity troubleshooting on mobile platforms
  • ROS 2 / real-time Linux, MCAP or similar log formats, and robot data infrastructure
  • MES/manufacturing data systems, station data pipelines, and yield dashboards
  • Test automation at scale — HIL rigs, automated regression on physical hardware, fleet dashboards

At Meta, we're building the future of human connection and the technology that enables it, continuously inventing for the next generation of experiences. To move toward advanced machine intelligence, we're enabling AI to go beyond vision and interact with the physical world. As we move closer to a future with intelligent robots and advanced AI models, we're hiring talent across robotics hardware, system software, machine perception, and artificial intelligence. You'll tackle open problems in robotics and AI, with the opportunity to shape new ways people connect around the world. We build complex electromechanical hardware, and the parts that move are the highest-risk elements of any program. This role owns failure analysis for hardware that fails design-verification, qualification, and production testing — from first symptom through root cause to a documented, transferable corrective action. You will work in the lab with hardware in your hands, in the data with logs and telemetry, and across electrical engineering, firmware, mechanical engineering, and quality teams to close the loop on defects before they reach a product. Scope spans actuators and drive systems, precision mechanisms, sensors, and the electronics and firmware that control them.

Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end FA for units failing fixture, DVE, and qualification testing: intake, symptom capture, hypothesis-driven teardown, root cause, disposition, and corrective-action follow-through
  • Build and maintain a failure-mode taxonomy for the hardware in scope and classify incoming failures against it, so root causes transfer between units instead of being re-derived every time
  • Diagnose by signature, not by guesswork — isolate the failing domain (mechanical, electrical, firmware, thermal, process) using periodicity, load-vs-position behavior, electrical waveforms, calibration and configuration data, and environmental correlation
  • Write and maintain analysis tooling (Python) that parses test-station reports and time-series logs to classify failure modes automatically at fleet/population scale
  • Run fleet-level correlation studies to accept or refute candidate root causes, and document refuted leads as clearly as confirmed ones
  • Drive nonconformance (NC) and CAPA workflows: file, triage, and close NCs; present findings at CCB / design review; feed pass-fail criteria improvements back into the test stations
  • Partner with design ME/EE/FW on containment and permanent fixes, and with suppliers on incoming quality and process escapes
  • Perform and interpret physical FA: precision teardown, dimensional/metrology inspection, wear and fracture surface inspection, optical/microscopy, and — where available — CT, SEM/EDX, and cross-sectioning

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 5+ years of hands-on failure analysis, reliability, or test engineering on electromechanical hardware (motors and drives, gearboxes, precision mechanisms, consumer devices, instrumentation, or similar)
  • Demonstrated root-cause methodology: 5-Why, fishbone, fault-tree, DOE, or equivalent, applied to real hardware failures you can talk through in detail
  • Hands-on lab competence: DMM, oscilloscope, power supplies, load/test fixtures, DAQ
  • Experience writing technical FA reports that enable design engineers to act on findings without additional clarification — FA reports that a design engineer can act on without a meeting

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with motor control and firmware concepts: commutation, field-oriented control, current limits, calibration tables, and encoder error sources
  • Working knowledge of BLDC/PMSM motors, gear trains, bearings, brakes, and position encoders
  • Working knowledge of quality systems: 8D, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, MSA/Gage R&R
  • Experience taking electromechanical assemblies — robotic joints and actuators, or comparable precision hardware — from prototype through DVT/PVT into production
  • Experience querying and building on large test-data pipelines and dashboards
  • Reliability engineering depth: HALT/HASS, Weibull and life-data analysis, rainflow/duty-cycle load-spectrum analysis, accelerated life testing
  • Experience with metrology and analytical FA labs (CT, SEM/EDX, metallography, tribology)

As an Analyst in Meta’s Competitive Intelligence organization, you will operate at the intersection of analytics, data science, and market strategy. You will work on major projects and product areas (often in environments of significant ambiguity or technical complexity) to drive both technical and business outcomes. This is a hands-on, high-impact role for builders who thrive on solving real problems. This role demands a unique blend of analytical and statistical knowledge, strategic thinking, and the ability to translate complex insights into impactful product and business decisions. You will be recognized as a thought partner by cross-functional leads and will help shape the analytical foundations that inform how we build and grow our products.

Responsibilities

  • Market Strategy: Influence organization-level product direction through data-driven narratives and an in depth understanding of the competitive landscape.
  • Demonstrated experience operating at scale, and across ambiguous, environments with working knowledge of econometrics.
  • As a quantitative market-strategist, you will blend practical and applied understanding with technical expertise, including pressure-testing data for quality, reliability, understanding data biases and being solution-driven.
  • Analytics Leadership: Conduct analyses with 3P datasets, develop statistical models and forecasts, and deliver actionable insights that inform market and business strategy.
  • These include, but are not limited to:
  • Data onboarding: Identify, onboard, and rigorously evaluate 3P datasets to determine their signal-to-noise ratio and predictive power.
  • Data triangulation: Triangulate data from many sources of imperfect information.
  • Synthesize multiple, low-fidelity 3rd-party signals into a single high-fidelity trend report using Bayesian aggregation or other methods.
  • Data transformation: Apply quasi-experimental designs (e.g., synthetic control, diff-in-diff) to isolate the impact of exogenous market shocks and competitor actions on internal performance metrics, using 3rd-party behavioral and economic datasets Insight and implications: Apply guidance from analyses to increase the accuracy of forecasts and better understand market trends.
  • Technical & Methodological Knowledge: Demonstrated knowledge in relevant technical or methodological areas (e.g., causal inference, bayesian aggregation), driving the adoption of appropriate methods and organization-wide best practices that raise the bar for the entire team.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelors degree and a minimum of 4 years of work experience (minimum of 2 years with a Ph.D.) in business intelligence, product analytics, or economic / strategy consulting in a technology environment with increasing scope and impact
  • Demonstrated skill to ethically source, validate, and synthesize high-signal insights from people (e.g., stakeholder interviews, skilled conversations, field research, and relationship-based information gathering) while maintaining high standards for privacy, consent, and integrity
  • Proficiency in AI-powered tools: Demonstrate working knowledge of Generative AI technologies (e.g., LLM and AI agents) and experience designing, prompting, and orchestrating AI systems (e.g., prompt engineering) to automate data analyses, synthesize insights, and execute multi-step analytical tasks (e.g., prompting agent to clean datasets, build visualizations)
  • Practical working understanding of data-analytics tools, and direct experience managing, analyzing, manipulating and interpreting 1P and external 3P datasets
  • Experience with data querying languages (e.g., SQL), scripting languages (e.g., Python), and/or statistical/mathematical software (e.g., R)
  • Experience with statistical analysis, including causal inference (e.g., randomized control trials, quasi-experimentation such as synthetic control, diff-in-diff, meta-analyses) and/or bayesian aggregation (e.g., bayesian pooling, hierarchical modeling)
  • Demonstrated communication skills and experience presenting complex findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Demonstrated experience thriving in ambiguous environments and shaping new analytics organizations or products

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's or Ph.D. Degree in a quantitative field such as Quantitative Economics or Political Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Computer Science, Physics, Business, or Mathematics
  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies

Our teams’ mission is to explore, develop and help productionize high-performance software & hardware technologies for AI at datacenter scale. We achieve this via concurrent design and optimization of many aspects of the system from models and runtime all the way to the AI hardware, optimizing across compute, network and storage. The team invests significantly into model optimization on existing accelerator systems and guiding the future of models and AI HW at Meta. This drives improved performance, new model architectures and reduces cost of ownership for all key AI services at Meta: Recommendations and Generative AI. This is an exciting space that spans exploration and productionization, coupled with close collaborations with industry, academia, Meta’s Infrastructure and Product groups. Collaborating closely with product teams, the team's mode of operation is going from ideation and rapid prototyping, all the way to assisting productionization of high leverage ideas, working with many partner teams to bring learnings from prototype into production. In addition to the real-world impact on billions of users of the Meta products, our team members have won Best Paper Awards at prestigious conferences such as ISCA, ASPLOS, SOSP, and OSDI, with multiple papers selected for IEEE Micro Top Picks. We regularly publish in ICML, NeurIPS, SC, HPCA, NSDI, VLDB, MLSys, and more. Overall, our work largely corresponds to the research communities of systems in general and especially systems for ML (MLSys, SOSP, OSDI, SIGCOMM, NSDI), computer architecture (ISCA, ASPLOS, MICRO, HPCA), and ML (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR). You will operate at the intersection of offensive security thinking and privacy engineering, partnering with product, legal, policy, and engineering teams to surface and remediate privacy vulnerabilities at scale.   • Identify gaps in existing privacy controls, detection capabilities, and engineering processes, and drive technical solutions to close those gaps at scale

  • Experience designing and executing privacy or security red team assessments, including threat modeling, attack simulation, and control validation across large-scale consumer products
  • Experience identifying and exploiting privacy vulnerabilities such as re-identification risks, data minimization failures, unauthorized data access patterns, or consent and purpose limitation bypass

As a Sustaining Reliability Engineer at Meta Reality Labs, you will set the technical direction for the long-term reliability and quality of consumer hardware products after launch across Meta's device portfolio, including virtual reality headsets, augmented reality glasses, and wearable devices. In this role, you will own reliability engineering strategy for the installed base and for products scaling in manufacturing, from launch through end of life, and you will drive systemic resolution of field failures to root cause and corrective action across product families. You will define the metrics, methodologies, and reaction frameworks the organization uses to sustain field performance, influence design and architectural decisions on current and next-generation products, and partner with and influence cross-functional leaders and external suppliers. You will be a recognized technical authority who leverages data to identify population-based reliability and quality risks in both the factory and the field, and who mentors and elevates other engineers across the function.

Responsibilities

  • Own the reliability and quality engineering strategy and metrics (field return rate, failure rate, and quality KPIs) for all products actively out in the market or currently scaling in manufacturing, from launch through end of life, and set the bar for what good looks like across the portfolio
  • Drive systemic resolution of field performance issues, component obsolescence, and return-rate (RMA/warranty) optimization to root cause and corrective action, in partnership with cross-functional internal and external partners, including recurring and cross-product failure modes
  • Partner with and influence internal leaders and external suppliers to ensure long-term hardware field performance, and close the loop by institutionalizing lessons learned into design, NPI, and supplier processes
  • Define and own the field signal analytics, product health telemetry, and failure-reaction frameworks the organization relies on; set thresholds and escalation triggers for products in the field
  • Establish the standards, methodologies, and metrics for sustaining reliability and quality, including ongoing reliability testing (e.g., ORT), excursion/ECO assessment, post-ramp qualifications (PRQ) and change control against reliability and quality goals
  • Lead complex, multidisciplinary root cause analysis for reliability and quality escapes, distinguishing between design, material, manufacturing-process, and use-condition contributors, and drive corrective actions to closure
  • Provide Design-for-Reliability and architectural evaluations that carry field and sustaining learnings into new product categories and next-generation designs
  • Own the quality management system for products in sustaining; understand, analyze, and resolve field quality issues and influence internal teams to drive durable quality improvements
  • Translate reliability and quality data into risk assessments, reports, and positions that inform executive product and business decisions
  • Mentor and technically guide reliability and quality engineers across the function, raising the capability of the team

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Materials, or Electrical Engineering, a relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience

Meta's Data Center Project Development organization is seeking a Lease Connectivity Engineer to support the design and construction of network and power connectivity infrastructure for leased data center facilities. Our leased data center portfolio is a critical component of Meta's global compute infrastructure, enabling the scale and reliability required to support billions of users. In this role, you will serve as a subject matter expert on connectivity systems — including fiber, power, and network infrastructure — bridging the gap between landlord-provided facilities and Meta's technical requirements. You will collaborate with internal engineering teams, external landlords, utilities, and carriers to ensure seamless, on-time delivery of connectivity capacity.

Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end connectivity design and delivery for leased data center facilities, including fiber optic infrastructure, dark fiber procurement, carrier interconnection, and power utility coordination from site selection through commissioning
  • Serve as the primary technical liaison between Meta's network engineering teams, real estate and leasing teams, landlords, colocation providers, and external carriers to define and validate connectivity requirements for leased sites
  • Develop and review connectivity design packages, including pathway and conduit routing, meet-me room layouts, demarcation point specifications, and fiber plant documentation for leased and colocation facilities
  • Evaluate landlord and carrier proposals for technical compliance with Meta's connectivity standards, providing detailed gap analyses and negotiating technical remediation plans
  • Manage connectivity project schedules and milestones across multiple concurrent leased facility projects, proactively identifying risks to on-time delivery and driving resolution with internal and external stakeholders
  • Coordinate with utility providers and telecommunications carriers on service agreements, construction timelines, and technical specifications to ensure adequate power and fiber capacity at leased sites
  • Collaborate with construction management, network engineering, and operations teams to oversee installation, testing, and acceptance of connectivity infrastructure, including OTDR testing, fiber certification, and end-to-end circuit validation
  • Develop and maintain connectivity standards, design templates, and technical specifications for leased data center environments, incorporating lessons learned and evolving network requirements
  • Provide technical oversight during construction administration phases, reviewing submittals, responding to requests for information, and conducting site walks to verify connectivity infrastructure installation quality

  • Experience coordinating with telecommunications carriers, dark fiber providers, and utility companies on service delivery, technical specifications, and construction timelines
  • Experience reviewing and interpreting connectivity design drawings, specifications, and construction documents including pathway plans, fiber schedules, and meet-me room layouts
  • Experience managing multiple concurrent infrastructure projects across geographically distributed leased or colocation data center sites
  • Knowledge of data center power and network infrastructure standards, including ANSI/TIA, BICSI, and relevant building codes applicable to critical facility connectivity systems

  • Experience with colocation and leased data center contract structures, including technical annexes, service level agreements, and landlord connectivity obligations

Meta seeks a talented product attorney to serve as Associate General Counsel supporting Meta Robotics Studio. This role is product-focused and will involve close coordination with engineering, machine learning, hardware, policy, and other cross-functional partners to advise on a broad range of issues globally as we build robots. Almost nothing about this work has been done before. Robotics law is largely unwritten, and the questions this role takes on will often have no precedent, no settled guidance, and no playbook to work from. We are looking for an attorney who finds that energizing rather than unsettling: someone who reasons from first principles, gets comfortable fast with hard technical subject matter, and can chart a path forward through ambiguity. You will build the frameworks rather than inherit them, and what you build becomes how the program operates. This is a multi-year commitment and a rare chance to own a program's legal foundation from the beginning. We are looking for a candidate who has a solid understanding of laws and principles as they apply to consumer hardware and AI products, is motivated, collaborates well, and can practically weigh and manage legal risks.

  • Take on novel legal questions with no clear answer, reason them through from first principles, and deliver practical, strategic advice our product and engineering teams can act on
  • Analyze new products, features, and business models to identify and mitigate legal risks across multiple jurisdictions
  • Advise on a broad range of legal subject areas, including AI regulatory, hardware, trade, consumer protection, data protection, privacy, competition, intellectual property, product safety, workplace safety and emerging legal frameworks
  • Advise machine learning teams on dataset and model licensing, provenance, third-party model use, and how evolving global AI regulation applies to model development and data collection
  • Carry the hardware program's legal arc from prototype through development to manufacturing at scale, including product safety, certification, trade, and supply-chain risk, in partnership with our specialists
  • Evaluate, draft, and negotiate contracts relating to strategic partnerships, manufacturing and supply, data collection, and services integrated into our products
  • Work directly with product and technical teams to build your product knowledge and use that knowledge to provide front-line legal and strategic business advice across multiple jurisdictions
  • Drive high-profile, high-impact projects involving legal analysis and compliance with cross-functional stakeholders and subject matter experts both within Meta's legal department (such as privacy, product safety, trade, and IP) and across the business (such as policy, communications, and marketing) to analyze and communicate legal risks
  • Build the frameworks, playbooks, and templates that let this function scale, and build influential relationships with executives and product teams across Reality Labs
  • Influence product and business decisions, ensuring alignment with legal and regulatory requirements
  • Proactively identify and address potential legal roadblocks, developing plans to mitigate risks

  • 8+ years of legal experience as a practicing attorney, including at a law firm, in-house, or in government
  • Demonstrated ability to work in the face of ambiguity and to reason from first principles where precedent and settled guidance do not exist
  • Demonstrated experience providing legal advice on technology, internet, or media products and services

  • 5+ years of in-house experience advising product and engineering teams directly
  • Experience advising media, internet, or technology companies, preferably robotics, consumer electronics, wearables, automotive, or on-device AI
  • Experience taking a physical product from prototype to volume manufacturing, including product safety and certification
  • Experience advising on model development and training, dataset licensing and provenance, AI/ML governance, and emerging AI regulation
  • Substantial privacy and data protection experience, including consent mechanisms and connected-device and sensor data
  • Demonstrated legal and business judgment, technical acumen, and strategic thinking, along with experience working independently and cross-functionally

We are building a governance, risk, and compliance function to enable our company to build products that can withstand regulatory scrutiny, and to ensure Meta continues to meet global regulatory requirements and manage risk. Within the Regulatory Compliance Programs team, the Examinations & Audit (E&A) team owns Meta's readiness for, and execution of, external audit engagements — including the independent audit required under the EU Digital Services Act (DSA) — and operates at the intersection of policy, legal, engineering, and product. We are seeking a candidate to serve as E&A's most senior technical authority on control identification, technical response development, and evidence production across Meta's external audit portfolio. This is a portfolio-level role: rather than owning a single engagement, you will set the technical strategy that determines how Meta evidences regulatory compliance across multiple concurrent audits and regulatory regimes, and you will be accountable for whether that strategy holds up under independent testing. This is both a technical program and project management role. You should be able to read a system design, follow a data flow, and reason about whether a given log, pipeline, config, or metric can withstand independent testing — then drive the cross-functional work to make it so. At this level you are expected to do that at scale: establishing the evidence and control standards other teams build to, resolving the hardest and most ambiguous testability problems, and acting as the authoritative translation layer between external auditors and the engineering organizations whose systems are under examination.

Responsibilities

  • Set the technical strategy for how Meta identifies, designs, and evidences controls across the E&A audit portfolio, spanning multiple regulatory regimes and concurrent engagements.
  • Define the control architecture that maps regulatory obligations to the specific systems, pipelines, configurations, and enforcement mechanisms that implement them — and establish the standards other teams and subject matter leads build to.
  • Own Meta's technical position on the most complex and contested auditor requests: determining what evidence exists, what it actually demonstrates, where it is authoritative, and how it must be presented to withstand independent testing.
  • Serve as Meta's senior technical voice with external auditors, regulators, and independent assessors, coordinating Meta's technical position and submissions across engagements.
  • Direct technical evidence production across the portfolio — scoping, sequencing across engineering and data teams, and validating that deliverables meet auditor expectations at first submission.
  • Drive remediation of the most significant findings, holding accountable engineering and product owners to management action plans (MAPs) through to closure.
  • Own maturation of E&A's control framework — control objectives, testing methodologies, and evidence standards — so that annual audit cycles are repeatable and scale as the regulatory portfolio expands.
  • Scale audit and compliance effectiveness using AI to deliver monitoring, oversight, artifact generation, and org-wide continuous improvement; develop and deliver an AI-native approach to evidence gathering and control testing.
  • Design the tooling, automation, and reporting architecture that gives leadership visibility into audit status, control health, evidence readiness, and remediation progress.
  • Build consensus and buy-in across Product, Engineering, Legal, Policy, Data Science, Operations, and Internal Audit on control ownership and evidence obligations, surfacing risk and dependencies early with clear mitigation and escalation paths.
  • Maintain an in-depth understanding of the evolving regulatory landscape affecting Meta — including Integrity, Youth, Privacy, and Security — and translate it into audit and control strategy.
  • Mentor and develop technical program managers and subject matter leads across the team, raising the technical bar of the function.

  • Experience setting the technical strategy for, or leading, multiple concurrent regulatory audit programs or external assessments (e.g., SOC, ISO, DSA, or government/regulatory audits). Meta is seeking a Network Engineer to join our Site Services and Edge Network Services (ENS) Operations team with a focus on Outside Plant (OSP) infrastructure. In this role, you will support the deployment, integration, and ongoing operational health of OSP network infrastructure including long-haul fiber, metro fiber routes, conduit systems, and interconnection facilities across Meta's global network. You will work at the intersection of fiber optic transmission, physical layer systems, and route engineering to ensure reliable connectivity for hyperscale data center and backbone environments. Collaborating with network design, engineering, and cross-functional partners, you will help drive scalable OSP deployment strategies, resolve complex network incidents, and improve operational processes that underpin one of the world's largest and most dynamic network infrastructures.

  • Partner with network design and engineering teams to provide field-level feedback that informs future OSP route designs, fiber specifications, and scalability requirements

  • International and domestic travel may be required up to 25% of the time depending on business needs

  • Experience working with cross-functional teams and external vendors to execute OSP network deployments, fiber route builds, or incident resolution at scale
  • 2+ years of experience deploying, operating, or supporting large-scale Outside Plant infrastructure including long-haul fiber, metro fiber networks, and optical transmission systems
  • Experience analyzing operational datasets or metrics to identify trends, prioritize issues, and support data-driven decision making in a network operations context

Meta is seeking a System Failure Analysis Engineer to join our Hardware Quality and Reliability Engineering team, focusing on Early Field Failure Analysis (EFFA) and Ongoing Field Failure Analysis (OFFA) for consumer hardware products including virtual reality headsets, augmented reality glasses, and wearable devices. In this role, you will investigate hardware failures from field returns and customer-reported issues, identify root causes, and drive corrective actions that improve product quality and reliability. You will leverage strong software development skills and AI tool-building capabilities to create automated analysis solutions and intelligent diagnostic systems. You will partner closely with hardware design, manufacturing, field support, and reliability engineering teams to ensure Meta's next-generation devices meet the highest standards of performance and durability.

  • Perform Early Field Failure Analysis (EFFA) and Ongoing Field Failure Analysis (OFFA) on returned or customer-reported hardware units across Meta's consumer device portfolio, including VR headsets, AR glasses, and wearable electronics
  • Build and deploy AI-powered tools and machine learning models to automate failure classification, root cause prediction, and anomaly detection in field failure data
  • Develop software scripts, data pipelines, and analysis tools using Python or similar languages to streamline failure analysis workflows and improve diagnostic efficiency
  • Apply fault isolation techniques such as electrical characterization, boundary scan, and functional diagnostics to identify failure modes at the board, component, and system level
  • Conduct physical failure analysis using tools such as optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy, cross-sectioning, and X-ray inspection to determine root cause
  • Design and implement automated test and diagnostic systems that leverage AI and machine learning to enhance failure detection and triage capabilities

Meta is seeking a Director, Hardware Supply Chain Planning to serve as a senior individual contributor for server rack and component planning across Meta’s infrastructure supply chain. This is an individual contributor role with no people management responsibilities. This role owns the technical direction of how we plan, constrain, and commit tens of billions of dollars of server rack and component supply annually, balancing capacity, flexibility, supply capability, and cost, from base components to finished racks, in an environment of continual product introduction. We do this primarily by building software and mathematical optimization models, not manual planning. The person in this role is the senior technical lead whom cross-functional leadership trusts and from whom the planning team takes technical direction. They set the methodology, arbitrate the hard modeling and prioritization calls, steer supply feasibility runs and significant plan revisions end to end, and personally carry out the analyses that leadership relies on to make multi-billion dollar commitments. Influence here comes from technical credibility and judgment rather than reporting lines: this role routinely aligns Director- and VP-level partners across Infra, Sourcing, Finance, and Hardware Engineering on a single plan of record. This is a high-ambiguity, high-leverage role at the center of Meta’s AI and data center scaling strategy: millions of servers, gigawatts of capacity, and current-generation silicon. If you are passionate about optimizing complex systems, working with large datasets and supply chains, and driving company-level business impact as a technologist rather than a manager, we encourage you to apply.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the senior technical authority for server rack and component supply planning: own the planning methodology, the models behind it, and the definition of what a credible plan is
  • Steer supply feasibility runs and significant plan revisions end to end: frame the scenarios, set the constraints and prioritization logic, arbitrate the trade-offs, and stand behind the answer with leadership
  • Deeply understand end-to-end planning processes, methodologies and data, and personally own delivery of an executable and optimized supply chain plan for racks and components
  • Critique the demand signals curated by upstream teams and build the anticipatory demand view for racks and components through mathematical modeling and business judgement, rather than treating the incoming signal as given
  • Identify capacity and supply chain risk proactively, and build the mathematical models behind simulation and optimization studies of demand projections, scenario planning, and gap closure analysis, driving the supply flexibility and optionality strategy that best balances delivery of required capacity, cost, and risk
  • Design and build the software and optimization systems that replace manual planning, contributing code yourself and partnering with software engineers to scale it, and set the technical standards, patterns, and quality bar that the broader planning team builds to
  • Act as the final technical escalation point for critical supply chain exceptions in racks and components: diagnose the root cause, decide on the recovery, and ensure the fix lands in the model and the process rather than in a one-off spreadsheet
  • Partner across Infra - platform teams, server hardware engineering, network engineering, data center engineering, operations, capacity planning, network planning, data center planning, energy - to find the most optimal ways to build and scale our infrastructure
  • Partner with Sourcing and suppliers on supply capability, lead times, commitment structures, and flexibility, translating commercial constructs into planning logic and vice versa
  • Partner with Finance to balance cost efficiency with technical, product, and supply chain considerations, and to connect the supply plan to budget, capex, and long-range planning
  • Represent the plan and its assumptions directly to senior leadership: make the recommendation, expose the risk honestly, and drive the decision to closure
  • Define, measure, and improve the metrics that determine whether the plan is good: feasibility, accuracy, cycle time, cost, and risk exposure
  • Raise the technical bar of the planning organization through design review, mentorship, and hands-on coaching of engineers on modeling, data, and problem framing (technical mentorship; no direct reports)
  • Influence and interweave technology strategy and product transitions into the planning models, anticipating where planning needs to be in two to three years (new silicon, new rack architectures, new supply chain constructs) and driving the technical investments to get there

  • Experience designing or co-designing imaging hardware and sensor systems, including knowledge of optics, image signal processing pipelines, and sensor physics

We are seeking a Security Risk Program Manager to build one of the program's highest-priority new capabilities: security risk assessment of AI product launches. Today, AI launches receive ad-hoc coverage through security risk assessments designed for infrastructure — not for product-launch cadence, and not for cross-domain AI risk spanning Security, Privacy, Integrity, and Legal. You will design that capability from the ground up and scale it from roughly five assessments per quarter today to twenty or more per quarter by H1 2027, in step with Meta's AI product velocity. This is a builder and an influencer role in equal measure. AI launch risk cannot be assessed by one function acting alone — it requires Central Security, product groups, Privacy, Integrity, and Legal moving through a shared process on a launch timeline. You will own that operating model: translating product and engineering reality into a defensible risk position, and translating regulatory obligation into assessment work that product teams can actually absorb without stalling a launch. The ideal candidate is comfortable with ambiguity, effective in high-pressure and fast-moving situations, and able to build durable relationships across a wide range of technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Responsibilities

  • Design and implement Meta's AI Launch Risk Assessment framework end to end — intake criteria, cross-domain risk taxonomy, assessment methodology, and launch-gate outputs — and scale delivery from ~5 to 20+ assessments per quarter by H1 2027.

At Meta Reality Labs, we build world-class consumer virtual, augmented, and mixed reality experiences. You'll work alongside leading scientists and engineers on the technology that will make AR and VR pervasive — turning science fiction into products people use every day. The Advanced Photonics group within Display Systems Research (DSR) is hiring an Optical Scientist to push nano-photonics research toward wearable AR systems that enable advanced perceptual capabilities. In this role you will conceptualize, design, build, and validate immersive display, sensing, and optical-compute components and architectures. We're looking for someone with a first-principles understanding of nano-photonic devices — metastructures, optical computation, and visible/IR photonic integrated circuits — who is equally comfortable developing the simulation, optimization, and validation methods those devices demand, in a highly cross-functional and fast-moving environment.

  • Design and model component technologies and system architectures for near-eye display combiners, novel sensors, and optical compute
  • Advance our design methodologies and workflows, including strategic planning of new algorithms and expansion of simulation and optimization capabilities for future technologies and products

  • 8+ years experience in scientific programming and data analysis tools (e.g. MATLAB, Python, C++, etc.)
  • 8+ years experience with methods of light propagation both in wave and ray domains as well as mixed models and familiarity with local and global optimization algorithm development
  • Experience with wave optics, geometric optics, polarization, and coherence
  • 8+ years experience with electromagnetic modeling and analysis of nanoscale structures, anisotropic materials, non-linear materials, switchable materials or holographic elements
  • 8+ years of experience in fabrication and functional testing of novel photonic devices such as metastructures, photonic integrated circuits, holographic elements, diffractive, and refractive structures

  • 10+ years of experience in design, fabrication and testing of novel optical structures such as active or passive metastructures, holographic elements, sub-wavelength diffractive structures, beam steering elements, novel sensors, optical compute, etc
  • 10+ years experience in using machine learning or deep neural networks for novel nano-optics design
  • 10+ years experience in working with electromagnetic theory, modeling optical structures and building software tools for simulation work on distributed systems and parallel computing infrastructure

Meta's Robotics Supplier Development Engineering (SDE) team is looking for a **Supplier Development Engineer** to join our growing team. The SDE team sits at the critical juncture between innovative product design and scalable, high-volume manufacturing — bridging upstream development (product design, material selection) and downstream integration (FATP). You will take ownership of the technical and operational complexities of ramping robotics products from prototype through mass production. This is a unique opportunity to shape how Meta's next-generation robotics hardware gets built at scale. You'll work hands-on with suppliers, develop manufacturing processes, drive quality systems, and collaborate deeply with Hardware, Industrial Design, Process, Sourcing, FATP Operations. **Component & Module Scope** **Electromechanical:** Motors, Actuators, Gear Train **Mechanical:** Enclosures, Housings, Structural Components, Thermal Management, Softgoods **Electronics & Sensing:** Cables, Wire Harness, Connectors, PCBA/FPC, Tactile Sensing, Battery, Display **Audio & Vision:** Audio Modules, Camera/Sensor/Lens, Display, Optical Covers **Surface Finishing:** CMF/Functional Coatings & Finishes (Painting, Anodization, Specialized Coatings) **About the Team** The Robotics SDE team was established in 2026 under the Supply and Supplier Development Engineering organization. Our mission is to develop customized, scalable manufacturing processes and quality management systems that support Meta's robotics initiatives from prototype through production. We integrate four core functions — Manufacturing Design Engineering (MDE), Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE), Advanced Manufacturing Technology Development (AMTD), and Subject Matter Experts (SME) — to provide comprehensive technical oversight of our Tier 2 supply chain. We engage early with Hardware, Engineering, Process, and Sourcing teams to ensure that new technologies, manufacturing methods, and quality & inspection methodologies are seamlessly integrated at the component, sub-assembly, and module levels at scale. **Why Join Us** - **Founding team opportunity** — Help build and shape the SDE function for Meta Robotics from the ground up - **Cutting-edge hardware** — Work on next-generation robotics platforms (humanoid robots, actuators, sensing systems) - **End-to-end ownership** — Own the full manufacturing lifecycle from early design engagement to mass production ramp - **High impact** — Directly influence product architecture and supplier strategy for Meta's robotics programs - **Cross-functional depth** — Collaborate daily with world-class Industrial Design, Product Design, Mechanical Reliability & Safety, and sourcing teams

Responsibilities

  • **Manufacturing Process Development:** Develop optimized, scalable manufacturing processes for robotics components and modules — from component-level DFM through process bring-up and line qualification at supplier sites
  • **Quality Engineering:** Define quality characterization, inspection methodologies (FAI/CPK, MSA, OQC/IPQC/IQC), and qualification standards; oversee module qualification processes and production readiness milestone execution
  • **Tooling & Fixture Development:** Develop end-to-end process strategies and fixture/process bring-up solutions that provide a clear path to mass production
  • **Supplier Technical Management:** Assess supplier capabilities, equipment readiness, and scalability; contribute to SPOR (Supplier Plan of Record) scorecards and drive vendor capability development
  • **Design for Manufacturability (DFM):** Provide early DFM feedback to Product Design and Industrial Design teams, identify manufacturing process risks before architecture lock, and ensure design intent is preserved through production
  • **Cross-Functional Collaboration:** Partner with Hardware Engineering, Quality, Reliability, TPM, and Strategic Sourcing teams across all phases of the product development lifecycle
  • **Issue Resolution:** Debug manufacturing issues (yield, cosmetics, dimensions) at supplier sites from NPI through ramp; identify root causes and implement corrective actions, leverage AI to ensure preventive measures are in place

Minimum Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in supplier development, manufacturing engineering, or process engineering in a hardware product environment
  • Hands-on experience with manufacturing processes such as CNC machining, injection molding, die casting, sheet metal fabrication, surface finishing (painting, anodization, coating), or PCBA assembly
  • Demonstrated ability to drive DFM, process optimization, and quality improvement at supplier sites
  • Experience with GD&T, statistical process control (SPC/CPK), and measurement system analysis (MSA)
  • Strong understanding of NPI lifecycle from prototype (EVT/DVT/PVT) through mass production ramp
  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
  • Experience with failure analysis and troubleshooting cosmetic and functional coating defects
  • Experience managing multiple suppliers and/or multiple projects concurrently
  • Willingness to travel domestically and internationally (up to 25–40%) to supplier sites

  • Experience managing multiple concurrent NPI programs, including milestone tracking, risk communication, and cross-functional coordination
  • Proficiency with metrology equipment and inspection methodologies (CMM, optical measurement, CT scanning)
  • Experience with FMEA, 8D, and root cause analysis methodologies
  • Background in supplier qualification, audit, and capability assessment (SPOR/RFI evaluation)
  • Experience in robotics, consumer electronics, automotive, or medical device manufacturing
  • Experience managing multi-supplier programs and driving process standardization across vendors

Meta is seeking a Revenue Controllership Manager to join the controllership function, owning the governance and technical accounting foundation beneath a rapidly evolving revenue landscape spanning advertising, messaging, subscriptions, and other revenue streams. We're looking for a technically skilled, improvement-minded leader who brings judgment to ambiguous accounting questions, thinks in terms of risk and control rather than checklists, and can make a complex revenue issue clear with finance leadership and cross-functional partners. You will be responsible for the governance framework, control environment, and technical accounting positions across assigned revenue streams, while actively leveraging AI and automation to enhance the efficiency, accuracy, and scalability of how those controls operate. In this role, you will partner closely with cross-functional business partners, engineers, and the broader finance team, advising early on how new products, pricing models, and non-standard arrangements should be structured rather than accounting for outcomes after the fact. You will combine business acumen and governance foundation with technical accounting knowledge to influence outcomes across functions. This role is also built for someone eager to develop deep operational fluency in our revenue processes — and you will be supported in building that understanding on the job.

Responsibilities

  • Own and continuously improve the governance framework and control environment over assigned SOX revenue streams, including control design, documentation, monitoring, remediation, and narrative and evidence standards
  • Research, conclude, and document technical accounting positions under ASC 606 and related guidance for new products, pricing models, partner arrangements, and non-standard transactions
  • Maintain a risk rated inventory of new and emerging revenue products, prioritizing governance depth against the highest risk arrangements rather than applying uniform review to every launch, and escalate the resulting prioritization to Controllership leadership
  • Advise business partners early on deal and product structuring, providing a clear point of view on accounting consequences and proposing alternative structures that achieve business objectives with better accounting and control outcomes
  • Assess how upstream system and process changes affect revenue recognition and the control environment, and translate those effects into accounting and control requirements
  • Monitor developments in US GAAP affecting revenue recognition and drive the policy, process, and operational changes required to implement them; serve as a primary contact for Internal Audit and external auditors on revenue-related walkthroughs, testing, and remediation
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives across Finance, Product, Engineering, Tax, Legal, and Business Operations, driving alignment and outcomes through influence rather than direct authority
  • Build and deliver clear, well-structured presentations of technical accounting conclusions, control status, and emerging issues to Controllership leadership and senior cross-functional stakeholders — structuring the narrative, calibrating depth to the audience, and driving to a decision
  • Proactively surface and pilot ideas leveraging AI and automation to reduce manual effort and strengthen control monitoring and evidence collection

Minimum Qualifications

  • 8+ years of relevant experience in revenue accounting, technical accounting, controllership, or public accounting
  • Certified Public Accountant (CPA)
  • Big 4 audit, technical accounting, or risk advisory background
  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field
  • Technical accounting background with demonstrated knowledge of ASC 606, including experience researching and documenting technical accounting conclusions
  • Experience designing, documenting, or operating internal controls over financial reporting, including SOX
  • Experience advising business partners on transaction or arrangement structuring, including proposing alternatives to achieve a desired accounting outcome
  • Experience understanding complex products and systems-driven, high-volume transaction processes, and their related revenue accounting implications
  • Experience building and presenting materials on complex accounting or control topics to senior finance leadership, including structuring a narrative that drives to a recommendation
  • Experience communicating with cross-functional and senior internal audiences, with the ability to distill complex concepts and analysis into concise, actionable conclusions
  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and influencing outcomes without direct authority, while operating with ambiguity and exercising judgment on what requires control now versus later

Preferred Qualifications

  • Oracle ERP experience
  • Experience with data analysis, process automation, and working with AI, SQL, Python, or similar tools
  • Experience in a technology, advertising, payments, or subscription business with high-volume, systems-driven revenue
  • Experience with Google Sheets, Google Slides, Excel, PowerPoint, and data visualization tools such as Tableau or Google Data Studio
  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
